text:
Maria V.: Heads up — noticed dashboard LCP spikes on canary after the heatmap rollout, looks like a late import from a third-party lib is inflating bundle parse time. :eyes:
Devin K.: ugh, which import? stack traces?
Maria V.: `import 'heat-tiles/legacy-plot.js'` inside the new heatmap wrapper — webpack stayed lazy but it ends up in the main chunk because of a shared util. Parse + GC spike on client.
Sasha R.: that could explain the sudden 120ms main-thread parse bump. Any telemetry traces?
telemetry-bot: Sampled traces for route /dash/heatmap — 95th p75 main-thread parse increased from 38ms -> 162ms after canary at 2026-03-18T14:02Z.
Ian L.: Is this a bundling bug or routing policy misroute causing a heavyweight chunk to load on non-heatmap routes?
Devin K.: quick repro: open dashboard, switch to metrics pane — the chunk loads even when heatmap isnt visible because the router prefetch policy is set to `route-level: eager` + shared util prevents split.
Maria V.: Right. Prefetch + shared util + webpack common chunk = late heavyweight parse on many routes. We need either change prefetch policy or split the util.
Sasha R.: Options: 1) change prefetch rule for heatmap to `defer-until-visible`, 2) move the legacy plot into its own async boundary (split the util), 3) tune routing-quota to reduce concurrent preloads. Thoughts?
Ian L.: I'd prefer minimal blast radius: flip prefetch to defer in canary and see SLO impact. If p95 drops, follow up with proper code split.
Devin K.: Agree. Can we do a quick canary config change? Where is the rollout flag?
Maria V.: It's `console.rollouts.heatmap.prefetch` in feature-flags service. I can flip canary group to `defer` now.
Sasha R.: Ping the deploy bot when you flip, we should watch telemetry and CPU profiles.
Maria V.: flipping now — @deploy-bot start canary-update console-rollout heatmap-prefetch -> defer :rocket:
deploy-bot: Canary update started (id: cb-heatmap-prefetch-20260318). Target group: 10% users in eu/us.
telemetry-bot: Noted. Sampling windows will report within ~5m.
Devin K.: while that runs, let's add a quick client-side guard: if the heatmap container is hidden, avoid prefetch manually (cheap guard). Patch in a single line.
Ian L.: Throw the guard behind `if (window.__REDWOOD_LOW_LATENCY_EXP) {}` so we can roll back quick without a build.
Maria V.: pushed a small patch to canary branch with the guard. `client/heatmap/index.ts` add `if (!isVisible(container)) return;` before import().
Sasha R.: Perfect. Once canary stabilizes, we should also update the bundler config to force `heat-tiles` into a dedicated chunk (split-by-entry + splitChunks force).
Devin K.: Also check telemetry sampling — current sampling rate is 1% for main-thread parse. We should temporarily increase it to 10% for the canary window to get signal.
telemetry-bot: Sampling rate updated for route /dash/* from 1% -> 10% for 30m by Sasha R.
Maria V.: Canary metrics: p75 parse down to 46ms after flip, p95 down to 78ms. GC spikes reduced. Looks promising.
Ian L.: Nice. Rollout to 30% and keep increased sampling for another hour.
Sasha R.: I'll open a follow-up ticket to split the util and force chunking rules. Also add a small test that asserts no heavy chunk loads on non-heatmap routes (`maxChunkSizeOnRoute < 80kb`).
Devin K.: And add an ops alert: if main-thread parse delta > 50ms after a console deploy, auto-disable prefetch for the new route.
Maria V.: filing followups and tagging eng-sre. Thanks all — good quick win. :thumbsup:
Ian L.: tl;dr: lazy third-party import + eager prefetch -> widespread parse blowup; temporary guard + prefetch policy flip fixes canary; plan: code-split + bundler enforcement + sampling bump for rollout observability.
